decisions.reason: The cloud transactional email service is featured on the home page, a highly visible public commitment that fits the firm's announced cloud direction, so management will persist and treat any weak early results as start-up effects.

Having its own dedicated page signals meaningful investment and commitment, and document capture complements the firm's messaging services, so early disappointments are likely to be attributed to temporary market-entry causes.
Email and fax conversion is close to the firm's established messaging core and costs little to maintain, so management has little reason to reverse the decision after only one year.
This minor feature is only mentioned and has low visibility, but it is embedded in the fax offering and cheap to keep, so it will likely stay even though it is the easiest item to quietly drop.
Sandbox threat protection supports the firm's announced email security direction, and the investment in it would need justifying, so management will continue it.
Multi-engine virus scanning is central to the security portfolio alongside the sandbox, so dropping it within a year of launch would contradict the firm's public positioning.
